read_source.description:
Read the source of the file under test (line-numbered).

This tool becomes available after the mandatory initial ``read_tests``
call returns. Use it when coverage feedback does not contain enough
source context for a targeted edit, or to refresh after a context
trim. Pass ``start_line`` / ``end_line`` to page a file past the size
limit. An immediate consecutive whole re-read (no other tool call
between) returns a short cached header; calling any other tool resets
the counter.

read_tests.description:
Read your working file (line-numbered),
not the source under test (that is ``read_source``). Pass
``start_line`` / ``end_line`` to page a file past the size limit.

edit_tests.description:
Edit this agent's file by content match (no line numbers). Three
operations from one tool:

- Insert: anchor ``old_text`` on an existing unique line and put that
  same line plus the new code in ``new_text``. To add a block, anchor on
  the line above or below where it goes and include it in ``new_text``.
- Replace: ``old_text`` is the exact block to swap for ``new_text``.
- Delete: pass "" as ``new_text`` to remove the matched block.

``old_text`` must occur exactly once unless ``replace_all`` is set.
Copy whitespace and indentation exactly: CRLF is normalized to LF,
line numbers copied from the read and edit views (``42<TAB>``) and
markdown fences are stripped, and an
exact miss falls back to a whitespace-loose match that re-indents
``new_text`` to the file. The edit is rejected, and nothing is written,
on no match, a multi-match, an empty ``old_text``, a result that no
longer parses or that the target's parser rejects, a duplicate
definition, or a test that inspects the target's source or bytecode;
the file is unverified until the next ``run_tests``.

Several edits: pass ``edits``, a list of ``{old_text, new_text}``
items, each with an optional ``replace_all``, instead of ``old_text``
and ``new_text``. They apply in list order, each matched against the
file as the previous ones left it, and the checks run once on the
final result: all or nothing, and an error names the failing edit by
its position. Use the list for changes that depend on each other,
such as a new version of a test and the deletion of the old one, a
block header and its body, or swapping two names: one at a time, the
first of them would be rejected. Several separate edit_tests calls in
one reply also apply in call order, each against the file after the
previous calls.

Args:
    old_text: exact text to find; add surrounding context to make it
        unique. To insert, this is the anchor line you keep in new_text.
    new_text: replacement text, required for a single edit; ""
        deletes the matched block.
    replace_all: replace every occurrence instead of requiring one;
        in a list, set it on the item.
    edits: several edits applied in order as one change, with
        old_text and new_text left out.

run_tests.description:
Run the tests for the file you are editing and report green or red.

Returns a compact summary: pass / fail counts, the first failing
tracebacks, and any collection errors. A green run that emits
unsound-async warnings (unawaited coroutines, leaked tasks,
unraisable exceptions) is reported as RED -- a falsely-passing test
is not green. A byte-identical re-run with no edit since the last
call returns the cached result; edit the file first to make progress.

measure_coverage.description:
Measure line/branch coverage of the target file AND show the source
code of any uncovered lines/branches in one call.

The first part of the return is the numeric summary (line %, branch %,
missing-line count). The second part is the actual source code of the
uncovered regions with context, so you can write targeted tests
without needing a separate tool.

final_answer.name: emit_coverage_test_result
final_answer.description: Emit the final structured result for this run. Call this tool ONLY when you have everything you need to return; the args become the run's output.

result_fields.test_file_name: Filename of the on-disk working file (e.g. test_encoder.py).
result_fields.explanation: Brief explanation of test strategy and what is covered.
result_fields.line_coverage: [auto] Final line-coverage % from the last measure_coverage measurement.
result_fields.branch_coverage: [auto] Final branch-coverage % from the last measure_coverage measurement.
result_fields.test_count_standard: [auto] Number of test functions in the on-disk standard test file.
result_fields.test_loc_standard: [auto] Lines of code in the on-disk standard test file.
result_fields.target_loc: [auto] Lines of code in the target source file.
result_fields.target_complexity: [auto] Cyclomatic-style complexity proxy for the target source file.
result_fields.agent_iterations: [auto] Total tool calls made during this run.
result_fields.agent_duration_s: [auto] Wall-clock seconds spent in this generate_coverage_tests call.
result_fields.input_tokens: [auto] Total prompt tokens consumed across all model invocations in this run.
result_fields.output_tokens: [auto] Total completion tokens emitted across all model invocations in this run.
result_fields.cache_hit_tokens: [auto] Cached-prefix prompt tokens (provider prompt-cache hits), a subset of input_tokens.
result_fields.status: [auto] Outcome category: success | stagnation | tests_failed | context_overflow | budget_exhausted | agent_error.
result_fields.error: [auto] Error message when status is not success.

measure_mutation.description:
Run the mutation engine against the target source. The working
file is the one collectable suite, so its tests are the
kill-witnesses.

Returns mutation_score % plus killed / survived / timeout /
suspicious counts, plus a sample of surviving-mutant diffs when
the engine exposes them.

Stop semantics:
  - goal reached + post-goal patience exhausted -> framework
    synthesises MutationTestResult and ends the mutation phase
  - stagnation below goal (streak hits patience) +
    early_stop_on_stagnation -> same

final_answer.name: emit_mutation_test_result
final_answer.description: Emit the final structured result for this run. Call this tool ONLY when you have everything you need to return; the args become the run's output.

result_fields.mutation_test_file_name: Filename of the on-disk working file (e.g. test_encoder.py).
result_fields.explanation: Brief explanation of which surviving mutants you targeted and how.
result_fields.targeted_mutants: Ids of the surviving mutants the new tests target, as the survivor list shows them (the id after '--- mutant').
result_fields.mutation_switched: [auto] Whether the loop switched from the selective proxy to the full catalogue.
result_fields.mutation_selective_final: [auto] Selective-proxy score at the switch (null if no switch).
result_fields.mutation_full_at_switch: [auto] Full-catalogue score the moment the loop switched (null if no switch).
result_fields.test_count_mutation: [auto] Test functions in the revised delivered suite.
result_fields.test_loc_mutation: [auto] LOC in the revised delivered suite.
result_fields.agent_iterations: [auto] Total tool calls in this run.
result_fields.input_tokens: [auto] Total prompt tokens consumed across model invocations.
result_fields.output_tokens: [auto] Total completion tokens emitted across model invocations.
result_fields.cache_hit_tokens: [auto] Cached-prefix prompt tokens (provider prompt-cache hits), a subset of input_tokens.
result_fields.status: [auto] success | stagnation | budget_exhausted | agent_error | context_overflow | inconclusive | tests_failed | skipped.
result_fields.measured_suite_sha256: [auto] SHA-256 of the suite backing mutation_matrix.
result_fields.mutation_matrix: [auto] Latest complete full-catalogue matrix for phase-end reuse.
result_fields.measurement_identity: [auto] Target and instrument identity backing mutation_matrix.
